newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bank chip card users in global pact.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bank chip card users in global pact.

text.p: Licensees of Proton, the chip based stored-value payments card developed by Belgian banks, have set up an association to globally promote the product in the face of competition from rivals, such as Mondex and Visa.

"The formation of Proton World is a major step towards the establishment of a global standard for inter-operable smart card products," Guy Alloin, head of Belgian bank card company Banksys, said in a statement.
Proton is currently used by banks in Belgium, the Netherlands and Switzerland, among other countries. American Express has also licensed the technology.
Banksys said banks that participated in a first meeting of Proton World in Brussels last week included ABN-AMRO, Toronto Dominion Bank, Banco Santander Chile and Nordbanken AB.
Together they agreed to focus on joint marketing of Proton, new product development and global inter-operable standards.
Around 14 million Proton cards have so far been issued, of which one million in Belgium. Operator Banksys said that this would rise to 20 million by the end of 1997.

Proton cards, which use a microchip to store digital cash for small value payments in shops, restaurants and in vending machines, face strong competition in the global market for so-called electronic purse.

Rival products include Mondex, a stored-value card developed by major British banks but now majority-owned by MasterCard International, and a card developed by Dutch company DigiCash BV, which has been adopted by the Commercial Bank of Greece.
Visa International is also developing a smart card.
